# Plan 014: Within-Subject Temporal DIF + SIBTEST Availability

## Background

Plan_012 showed single-dimensional θ-conditioning cannot reduce the temporal cohort's
31% baseline FPR. Before launching a full bifactor model, we check whether the high
C% is driven by between-subject ability differences or within-subject DIF.

## Part 1: Within-Subject Temporal DIF

For each subject, MH-DIF uses **within-subject purified total score** as the matching
variable. This isolates DIF to items within the same content domain, removing
between-subject ability confounds.

### Results

| Subject | N items | ETS A | ETS B | ETS C | C% | A% |
|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|-----|-----|
| business_ethics | 93 | 32 | 19 | 42 | 45.2% | 34.4% |
| human_aging | 203 | 96 | 40 | 67 | 33.0% | 47.3% |
| formal_logic | 109 | 46 | 20 | 43 | 39.5% | 42.2% |
| professional_medicine | 248 | 124 | 47 | 77 | 31.1% | 50.0% |
| high_school_statistics | 181 | 66 | 39 | 76 | 42.0% | 36.5% |

**Average within-subject C%: 38.1%**

## Part 2: Cross-Subject Matching Comparison

Cross-subject matching uses total score on **all other subjects** (excluding the
current one) as the matching variable. This eliminates within-subject ability
contamination of the matching variable.

tool_args.old_string: Temporal DIF analysis decomposes benchmark score differences into three layers. \emph{Layer~1} (impact): overall ability differences between cohorts, removed by matching (Cohen's $d = -0.17$; matched C\% $= 28.9\%$, reducing unmatched 31.3\% by $\sim$2.4~pp). \emph{Layer~2} (DIF): item-level differences persisting after ability control---the 28--29\% floor across multiple matching methods, of which 92.4\% is item-specific (pseudo $R^2 = 0.0007$). \emph{Layer~3} (attribution): whether DIF reflects contamination, capability evolution, or training methodology shifts---beyond observational DIF analysis without training data access. The practical import is identical regardless of attribution: temporal DIF means the same benchmark score carries different meaning across model generations. The Simpson's paradox (\Cref{sec:temporal}) confirms DIF is associated with item properties rather than accuracy gains. Aggregate ranking is preserved ($\rho \approx 0.997$), but family-level profiles reveal systematic shifts (Llama-3: ${+}53$ median rank; Mistral: $-35$) that matter for pairwise model selection. Domain directionality (STEM favoring 2024 at 55.4\%, Humanities favoring 2023 at 64.4\%) describes where measurement properties shift without implying a specific cause.

tool_args.old_string: We propose that benchmark maintainers run temporal MH-DIF analysis whenever $\geq 500$ new models accumulate (a practical threshold reflecting current accumulation rates of $\sim$400--800 models/year on METABENCH), using cross-subject matching, with graduated action levels: (1)~\emph{Monitor} (C\% $< 15\%$); (2)~\emph{Flag} ($15\% \leq$ C\% $< 25\%$): report stable-item rankings alongside full rankings; (3)~\emph{Act} (C\% $\geq 25\%$): investigate flagged items and report stable-item rankings, as exemplified by MMLU-Pro~\citep{wang2024mmlupro} and MMLU-Redux~\citep{gema2024mmlu}. MMLU's C\% exceeds the action threshold; these thresholds adapt ETS practice where C\% $\geq 25\%$ triggers item review, and the effect-size basis makes them portable across examinee populations~\citep{clauser1998dif}.
